summary: Bounded remediation of src/content/blog/beginner/short-head-line-meaning.md per revision 2: removed/narrowed four unsupported prevalence/consensus phrases ('popular palmistry most frequently distorts', 'most commonly distorted', 'generally treated as short', 'rarely the most decisive one on its own'), replaced vague-authority framing ('the tradition warns against', 'the careful tradition says', 'The tradition does not treat...', 'The tradition reads length...') with named Benham/Gettings attribution or neutral Palmistry Path editorial wording, and narrowed the source footer from all five house sources to only Benham and Gettings, the two sources actually consulted/supporting the retained claims. Preserved the accepted structure, navigation, core interpretation, and verified Benham quotation. No unrelated head-line interpretations, reciprocal link, or backlog bookkeeping changed.

source_preflight.notes: Re-ran the full preflight against the final revision-2 prose, not only the four named sentences. All four packet-named prevalence/superlative phrases were removed or rewritten without frequency/ranking language. Did not treat the identical unsourced sentence already present in 03-head-line.mdx ('popular palmistry most frequently distorts') as evidence for the article's own claim, per remediation item 3; it was independently removed here. All four vague-authority 'the tradition says/warns/does not treat/reads' constructions were replaced with explicit Benham/Gettings attribution or neutral editorial framing ('this article measures...', 'this article treats...'); retained 'traditionally associated with' phrasing elsewhere in the article is the AGENTS.md-endorsed grounded-phrasing convention, not an anonymous-authority assertion, and was left unchanged as out of the named remediation scope. Source footer narrowed to Benham and Gettings only -- Cheiro, West, and Fincham are not named or drawn on anywhere in the article body, so listing them implied unverified support and was removed. The two claim-risk PREVALENCE_OR_CONSENSUS flags remaining after the edit ('most alarming' describing a beginner's reaction, and 'ranging widely across many' describing the long-line mental-style analogy already accepted in revision 1) are reader-framing/idiomatic phrasing, not frequency or consensus claims about palmistry practice, and were manually dispositioned as harmless. Quotation fidelity, combination-reading, and safety-boundary checks are unchanged from revision 1 and were re-verified: the two quoted phrases ('abundant mentality', 'kind to be estimated by the character and color of the line') remain verbatim-verified against docs/source-verification-log.md line 409; the 'Length in context' section still explicitly declines to assert an unsupported combination reading; the article continues to explicitly reject the short-line/low-intelligence and IQ inferences rather than asserting them, with no medical, legal, financial, or predictive-science claim introduced.
